start_here: Say to your AI: "My webhook missed event msg_1srOsB4mXhCqCVwAxYRNnpFZhb3; have Resend send it to webhook 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 again." It runs tool:replay-a-webhook-event.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it asks your email-sending account to deliver one event again and writes nothing of its own.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once, so its key is held in your vault under a name of yours (a key with full access). The key is never typed into the request.
2. Find the event with tool:list-webhook-events: its id starts msg_, and a failed status means it never reached your address.
3. Fix what answers at the webhook's address first, so the new delivery can arrive.

4. Say to your AI: "Replay event <msg id> on my Resend webhook <id>", and give the held key's name. It calls tools:run with tool tool:replay-a-webhook-event and {"key_name": "<that name>", "webhook_id": "<id>", "event_id": "<msg id>"}.
5. The account delivers that one event again at once, with its own id, time and signature. A receiver that keeps each event id once treats a second replay as a duplicate.

worked_examples.title: One failed event sent again
worked_examples.ask: Replay event msg_1srOsB4mXhCqCVwAxYRNnpFZhb3 on my Resend webhook 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: the row sends POST https://api.resend.com/webhooks/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011/events/msg_1srOsB4mXhCqCVwAxYRNnpFZhb3/replay with your key in the Authorization header and returns Resend's reply unchanged. The ids are a synthetic sample in the shape of Resend's replay-event reference.

drafted_from: tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json (its row) and Resend's replay-event reference (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/replay-event, read 2026-11-25)
